records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.console_panel.ConsolePanel.shutdown#2
records.source: There is deliberately no ``QThread.terminate()`` fallback. It used to be here, described as a last resort, and it was reached far more often than "last resort" suggests: `spacr.qt.ai.worker` queued `worker.finished -> thread.quit` to the GUI-affine QThread object, so the event that stops the thread sat behind this method's own `wait()` and the wait timed out on streams that had already finished. Terminating a thread that is running Python is `pthread_cancel`: if it dies holding the GIL the process stops making progress with every thread still alive, and if it dies inside Qt or PySide the heap is corrupt and the crash lands somewhere unrelated later. `bridge.drain_thread` parks a thread that will not stop instead, which keeps the "never destroy a running QThread" rule without buying it with undefined behaviour.
records.context: There is deliberately no ``QThread.terminate()`` fallback. It used to be here, described as a last resort, and it was reached far more often than "last resort" suggests: `spacr.qt.ai.worker` queued `worker.finished -> thread.quit` to the GUI-affine QThread object, so the event that stops the independent execution path sat behind this method's own `wait()` and the wait timed out on streams that had already finished. Terminating an independent execution path that is executing Python is `pthread_cancel`: if it dies holding the GIL the process stops making progress with every independent execution path still alive, and if it dies inside Qt or PySide the heap is corrupt and the crash lands somewhere unrelated later. `bridge.drain_thread` parks an independent execution path that will not stop instead, which keeps the "never destroy an executing QThread" rule without buying it with undefined behaviour.
records.translation: Il n’existe délibérément aucune solution de repli vers ``QThread.terminate()``. Elle se trouvait autrefois ici, décrite comme un "last resort", mais était atteinte bien plus souvent que cette expression ne le suggère : `spacr.qt.ai.worker` plaçait `worker.finished -> thread.quit` dans la file de l’objet QThread lié à la GUI. L’événement qui arrête le chemin d’exécution indépendant se retrouvait donc derrière le propre appel `wait()` de cette méthode, lequel expirait pour des flux déjà terminés. Arrêter de force un chemin d’exécution indépendant qui exécute Python revient à `pthread_cancel` : s’il meurt en détenant le GIL, le processus cesse d’avancer alors que tous ses chemins d’exécution restent actifs ; s’il meurt dans Qt ou PySide, le tas est corrompu et une erreur sans rapport survient plus tard. `bridge.drain_thread` met plutôt en attente un chemin d’exécution qui refuse de s’arrêter. La règle "ne jamais détruire un QThread en cours d’exécution" est ainsi respectée sans recourir à un comportement indéfini.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#14
records.source: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable and the module refuses to pretend they are. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)`` — 41% wider limits, which is the difference between catching a drift and not. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.
records.context: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable and the module refuses to pretend they are. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)`` — 41% wider limits, which is the difference between catching a drift and not. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.
records.translation: Les deux constantes robustes ne sont *pas* interchangeables et le module refuse de prétendre le contraire. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) vaut ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` ; ce facteur fait de la MAD d’un échantillon normal une estimation sans biais de son écart-type. Une étendue mobile vaut ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, soit la valeur absolue de la *différence* entre deux observations. Son échelle est donc ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` et sa médiane ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplier une étendue mobile médiane par 1.4826 surestime sigma d’exactement ``sqrt(2)`` — des limites 41 % plus larges, ce qui peut empêcher de détecter une dérive. Les deux constantes sont calculées ici à partir de ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` pour la même raison que c4 est calculé avec la fonction gamma.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.home#2
records.source: 1. **The first tab is everything, in the same categories as the rest.** Home is not a summary of the other tabs — it holds every app, at a density that fits one screen, banded by the *same* sections the category tabs use. It used to band them into Prepare / Run / Review instead, a second grouping that existed nowhere else: an app read as "Prepare" on the first tab and "Data" on the second, and adding a section meant editing two tables that could disagree. There is one table now (:data:`spacr.qt.app.APPS`) and both the bands and the tabs are computed from it, by the *registry*, and handed in — this widget takes ``categories`` and ``bands`` already grouped and does not know what a section means.

records.translation: 1. **Le premier onglet contient tout, dans les mêmes catégories que les autres.** Home n’est pas un résumé des autres onglets : il contient chaque application, avec une densité adaptée à une vue d’application, regroupée dans les *mêmes* sections que les onglets de catégories. Autrefois, il les regroupait plutôt sous Prepare / Run / Review, une seconde organisation inexistante ailleurs : une application apparaissait comme "Prepare" dans le premier onglet et "Data" dans le deuxième, et l’ajout d’une section imposait de modifier deux tables susceptibles de diverger. records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.load_source_payload#1
records.source: This is the whole of a preview load, written so it touches **no widget and no Qt object** and can therefore be handed straight to :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. It used to be the ``run`` method of a hand-rolled ``QThread`` that emitted two signals, which kept the panel's sampler warm by ordering ``enumerated`` before ``loaded``; returning both halves in one dict gets the same ordering for free, because the caller adopts the enumeration and installs the image in a single GUI-thread call.

It used to be the ``run`` method of a hand-rolled ``QThread`` that emitted two signals, which kept the panel's sampler warm by ordering ``enumerated`` before ``loaded``; returning both halves in one key-value mapping gets the same ordering for free, because the caller adopts the enumeration and installs the image in a single main GUI execution path call.
records.translation: Il s’agit de l’intégralité du chargement d’un aperçu, écrite de façon à ne toucher **aucun widget ni objet Qt** ; elle peut donc être confiée directement à :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. C’était auparavant la méthode ``run`` d’un ``QThread`` artisanal qui émettait deux signaux et maintenait l’échantillonneur du panneau prêt en ordonnant ``enumerated`` avant ``loaded``. Le renvoi des deux parties dans un seul mappage clé-valeur offre gratuitement le même ordre, car l’appelant adopte l’énumération et installe l’image lors d’un seul appel dans le chemin d’exécution GUI principal.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.motility_preview#3
records.source: **Units.** The assay converts pixels per frame into physical units with ``factor = (1 / pixels_per_um) * (60 / seconds_per_frame)`` and only when *both* are known; otherwise it reports ``px/frame``. A preview that printed "velocity 4.2" while the user was thinking in µm/s would be worse than printing nothing, so the calibration fields start **unset**, every velocity carries its unit, and while the calibration is unknown the panel says so in words instead of quietly borrowing the 1.78 px/µm default.
records.context: **Units.** The assay converts pixels per frame into physical units with ``factor = (1 / pixels_per_um) * (60 / seconds_per_frame)`` and only when *both* are known; otherwise it reports ``px/frame``. A preview that printed "velocity 4.2" while the user was thinking in µm/s would be worse than printing nothing, so the calibration fields start **unset**, every velocity carries its unit, and while the calibration is unknown the panel says so in words instead of quietly borrowing the 1.78 px/µm default.
records.translation: **Unités.** L’essai convertit les pixels par image en unités physiques avec ``factor = (1 / pixels_per_um) * (60 / seconds_per_frame)``, uniquement lorsque les *deux* valeurs sont connues ; sinon, il indique ``px/frame``. Un aperçu affichant "velocity 4.2" alors que l’utilisateur raisonne en µm/s serait pire que l’absence d’affichage. Les champs d’étalonnage commencent donc **non définis**, chaque vitesse porte son unité et, tant que l’étalonnage reste inconnu, le panneau l’indique explicitement au lieu d’emprunter silencieusement la valeur par défaut de 1.78 px/µm.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.preview_controls#47
records.source: The sample is **random but reproducible**: the seed is a stable digest of ``"<folder name>|<total sets>|<cap>|<nonce>"`` (:func:`sample_seed`), so the same plate at the same cap yields the same sets in this session, the next session, and on another machine or mount point — a preview can be described and returned to. It is deliberately *not* seeded from the clock or from ``hash()``, which is salted per process. Re-rendering never re-draws; only an explicit act does — changing the cap (which is in the seed) or calling :func:`~ImageSetSampler.reshuffle` (which bumps the nonce).
records.context: The sample is **random but reproducible**: the seed is a stable digest of ``"<folder name>|<total sets>|<cap>|<nonce>"`` (:func:`sample_seed`), so the same laboratory microplate at the same cap yields the same sets in this session, the next session, and on another machine or mount point — a preview can be described and returned to. It is deliberately *not* seeded from the clock or from ``hash()``, which is salted per process. Re-rendering never re-draws; only an explicit act does — changing the cap (which is in the seed) or calling :func:`~ImageSetSampler.reshuffle` (which bumps the nonce).
records.translation: L’échantillon est **aléatoire mais reproductible** : la graine est un condensat stable de ``"<folder name>|<total sets>|<cap>|<nonce>"`` (:func:`sample_seed`). La même microplaque de laboratoire avec la même limite produit donc les mêmes ensembles dans cette session, dans la suivante et sur une autre machine ou un autre point de montage ; un aperçu peut être décrit puis retrouvé. La graine ne provient délibérément *pas* de l’horloge ni de ``hash()``, dont le sel change à chaque processus. Un nouveau rendu ne tire jamais un nouvel échantillon ; seule une action explicite le fait — modifier la limite, qui participe à la graine, ou appeler :func:`~ImageSetSampler.reshuffle`, qui incrémente le nonce.

La version remplacée employait ``with sqlite3.connect(...) as connection``, qui valide la transaction mais ne ferme **pas** la connexion. records.source: ``foreign.run_import`` copies the imported rows into the canonical ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` table when nothing of anyone else's is there, so that a purely-imported project is readable by every spaCR tool. ``measure_crop`` *appends*, so the moment spaCR measures the same fields its rows land in that table beside theirs, in different columns, with nothing to tell a reader which population a row belongs to — and ``count_cell`` becomes the sum of the two.
records.context: ``foreign.run_import`` copies the imported rows into the canonical ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` table when nothing of anyone else's is there, so that a purely-imported project is readable by every spaCR tool. ``measure_crop`` *appends*, so the moment spaCR measures the same fields its rows land in that table beside theirs, in different columns, with nothing to tell a reader which population a row belongs to — and ``count_cell`` becomes the sum of the two.
records.translation: ``foreign.run_import`` copie les lignes importées dans la table canonique ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` lorsqu’aucune ligne d’une autre origine ne s’y trouve, afin que tous les outils spaCR puissent lire un projet uniquement importé. ``measure_crop`` *ajoute* des lignes : dès que spaCR mesure les mêmes champs de vision, ses lignes rejoignent les lignes importées dans cette table, dans des colonnes différentes, sans indiquer au lecteur à quelle population appartient chaque ligne — et ``count_cell`` devient la somme des deux.

records.label: spacr.runctx#2
records.source: **One run id, on every log line and every output.** A run used to be untraceable. The log said a field failed; the registry said an artifact existed; nothing connected them, so "show me everything from the run that produced this file" had no answer. :func:`run_context` mints one id, stamps it onto every :class:`logging.LogRecord` created anywhere in the process, writes a per-run JSONL log that :func:`read_run_log` reads back, and hands the *same* id to :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. A log line and an output can therefore be joined on ``run_id``, which is the whole point.
records.context: **One processing-session id, on every log line and every output.** A processing session used to be untraceable. The log said a field failed; the registry said an artifact existed; nothing connected them, so "show me everything from the processing session that produced this file" had no answer. :func:`run_context` mints one id, stamps it onto every :class:`logging.LogRecord` created anywhere in the process, writes a per processing session JSONL log that :func:`read_run_log` reads back, and hands the *same* id to :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. A log line and an output can therefore be joined on ``run_id``, which is the whole point.
records.translation: **Un identifiant de session de traitement sur chaque ligne de journal et chaque sortie.** Une session de traitement était autrefois impossible à retracer. Le journal signalait l’échec d’un champ de vision ; le registre signalait l’existence d’un artefact ; rien ne les reliait, si bien que « montre-moi tout ce qui provient de la session de traitement ayant produit ce fichier » n’avait aucune réponse. :func:`run_context` crée un identifiant, l’ajoute à chaque :class:`logging.LogRecord` produit dans le processus, écrit un journal JSONL par session que :func:`read_run_log` relit, puis transmet le *même* identifiant à :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. Une ligne de journal et une sortie peuvent donc être jointes sur ``run_id``, ce qui est précisément l’objectif.

records.label: spacr.train_compare#7
records.source: The settings that produced a run are *not* in the run folder: ``save_settings`` writes them to ``<src>/settings/train_test_<model_type>_<epochs>.csv`` as a ``Key,Value`` CSV. :func:`load_run` walks up from the run folder to find it — but only as far as the run's own project root, which the layout above makes identifiable: ``<src>`` is the folder the ``model/`` tree hangs off. An ancestor above that belongs to a different project, and reading it would report somebody else's settings as this run's provenance, so the settings diff would show differences nobody configured and the answer would depend on where in the filesystem the project happened to sit. See :func:`_owns_this_run`.
records.context: The settings that produced a processing session are *not* in the processing-session folder: ``save_settings`` writes them to ``<src>/settings/train_test_<model_type>_<epochs>.csv`` as a ``Key,Value`` CSV. :func:`load_run` walks up from the processing-session folder to find it — but only as far as the processing session's own project root, which the layout above makes identifiable: ``<src>`` is the folder the ``model/`` tree hangs off. An ancestor above that belongs to a different project, and reading it would report somebody else's settings as this processing session's provenance, so the settings diff would show differences nobody configured and the answer would depend on where in the filesystem the project happened to sit. See :func:`_owns_this_run`.
records.translation: Les réglages qui ont produit une session de traitement ne se trouvent *pas* dans son dossier : ``save_settings`` les écrit dans ``<src>/settings/train_test_<model_type>_<epochs>.csv`` sous forme de CSV ``Key,Value``. :func:`load_run` remonte depuis le dossier de la session pour le trouver, mais seulement jusqu’à la racine du projet propre à cette session, identifiable grâce à l’organisation ci-dessus : ``<src>`` est le dossier auquel l’arborescence ``model/`` est rattachée. Un ancêtre plus haut appartient à un autre projet ; le lire attribuerait les réglages d’un tiers à la provenance de cette session. La comparaison afficherait alors des différences que personne n’a configurées et le résultat dépendrait de l’emplacement du projet dans le système de fichiers. Voir :func:`_owns_this_run`.

records.label: spacr.training_basis#4
records.source: **Backward compatibility is the whole difficulty.** A settings CSV written before this exists in every user's project folder, and INVARIANTS §6 is the trap: a key *absent* from the dict means the pipeline falls back to its own default, which can differ from the GUI's, and nothing says so. Every rename here is therefore an alias, not a replacement — :func:`normalize_settings` translates the old name and the old *implicit* basis into the new explicit one, and a run from an old CSV does exactly what it did before.
records.context: **Backward compatibility is the whole difficulty.** A settings CSV written before this exists in every user's project folder, and INVARIANTS §6 is the trap: a structured-data name *absent* from the key-value mapping means the workflow falls back to its own default, which can differ from the GUI's, and nothing says so. Every rename here is therefore an alias, not a replacement — :func:`normalize_settings` translates the old name and the old *implicit* basis into the new explicit one, and a processing session from an old CSV does exactly what it did before.
records.translation: **La compatibilité ascendante constitue toute la difficulté.** Un CSV de réglages antérieur à cette fonction existe dans le dossier de projet de chaque utilisateur, et INVARIANTS §6 recèle le piège : un nom de donnée structurée *manquant* dans le mappage clé-valeur amène le flux de travail à reprendre sa propre valeur par défaut, qui peut différer de celle de la GUI, sans aucun avertissement. Chaque renommage est donc un alias et non un remplacement — :func:`normalize_settings` traduit l’ancien nom et l’ancienne base *implicite* vers la nouvelle base explicite ; une session de traitement issue d’un ancien CSV se comporte exactement comme auparavant.

records.label: spacr.training_basis.inapplicable_settings#1
records.source: Greyed, not removed. INVARIANTS §6: a key absent from the dict makes the pipeline fall back to its own default, which can differ from the value the module needs. A greyed control keeps its value and stops being editable; a deleted one changes the run.
records.context: Greyed, not removed. INVARIANTS §6: a structured-data name absent from the key-value mapping makes the workflow fall back to its own default, which can differ from the value the module needs. A greyed control keeps its value and stops being editable; a deleted one changes the processing session.
records.translation: Grisé, pas supprimé. INVARIANTS §6 : si un nom de donnée structurée manque dans le mappage clé-valeur, le flux de travail reprend sa propre valeur par défaut, qui peut différer de celle requise par le module. Un contrôle grisé conserve sa valeur et n’est plus modifiable ; un contrôle supprimé modifie la session de traitement.

records.label: spacr.utils.console_safe#1
records.source: Console decoration must never be able to end a run. No Windows codepage encodes spaCR's own output set -- ``▸`` (U+25B8) is absent from cp1252, cp437, cp850, cp932 *and* cp936, and the box-drawing frame is absent from cp1252 -- and neither does any of them encode the domain vocabulary that ends up in settings values, such as the parental strain ``Δku80`` or a ``µm`` voxel size. Printing either to a non-UTF-8 stream raises ``UnicodeEncodeError``, and on Windows that is the normal case the moment stdout is redirected: a batch-queue job, ``spacr-run``, a legacy console.
records.context: Console decoration must never terminate a run. Windows code pages do not encode every spaCR output character. For example, ``▸`` is missing from cp1252, cp437, cp850, cp932 *and* cp936, and cp1252 lacks the frame characters. Settings may also contain ``Δku80`` or ``µm``. Writing these values to a non-UTF-8 stream raises ``UnicodeEncodeError``. On Windows, this commonly occurs when stdout is redirected by a batch job, ``spacr-run``, or a legacy console.
records.translation: La décoration de la console ne doit jamais pouvoir interrompre une session de traitement. Les pages de codes Windows ne représentent pas tous les caractères produits par spaCR. Par exemple, ``▸`` manque dans cp1252, cp437, cp850, cp932 *et* cp936, tandis que cp1252 ne contient pas les caractères du cadre. Les réglages peuvent aussi contenir ``Δku80`` ou ``µm``. Écrire ces valeurs vers un flux non UTF-8 lève ``UnicodeEncodeError``. Sous Windows, cela se produit couramment lorsque stdout est redirigé par une tâche en lot, ``spacr-run`` ou une console historique.

records.label: spacr.zstack.stitch_planes#1
records.source: Each plane is compared with the plane below it, and the pairing is greedy and **one-to-one**: pairs are considered in descending IoU and a label may take part in at most one link. That is what stops two genuinely different objects that merely happen to overlap the same object in xy from being fused -- only the better match inherits the label, the other starts a new one. Any pair below ``iou_threshold`` is not linked at all.
records.context: Each image layer is compared with the image layer below it, and the pairing is greedy and **one-to-one**: pairs are considered in descending IoU and a label may take part in at most one link. That is what stops two genuinely different objects that merely happen to overlap the same object in xy from being fused -- only the better match inherits the label, the other starts a new one. Any pair below ``iou_threshold`` is not linked at all.
records.translation: Chaque couche d’image est comparée à celle située en dessous ; l’appariement est glouton et **univoque**. Les paires sont examinées par IoU décroissante et une étiquette ne peut participer qu’à un seul lien. Deux objets réellement distincts qui chevauchent par hasard le même objet en xy ne sont donc pas fusionnés -- seule la meilleure correspondance hérite de l’étiquette et l’autre en commence une nouvelle. Une paire sous ``iou_threshold`` n’est jamais liée.
